newsitem.title: UK: Russian Eurobond seen at up to $750 mln -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Russian Eurobond seen at up to $750 mln -dealers.

text.p: Russia's proposed Eurobond could be for up to $750 million, against the maximum $500 million previously mooted, syndicate managers said on Wednesday. "We heard the rumour out of New York last night (Tuesday) and have been able to establish that it will be increased (from $500 million)," said a syndicate chief at a top European bank in London. "$750 million would seem the next logial step."
The deal, to be lead managed by J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg, was widely expected to have a five-year maturity.
Spread talk has narrowed to 300-350 basis points over U.S. Treasuries as a series of economic presentations around the world has sparked huge investor interest.
The roadshows end in New York today. Dealers there said on Tuesday the Eurobond could be launched shortly after the final presentation.
"What we hear is that the managers at J.P. Morgan and SBC Warburg are going to get together right after the New York show and will try to on the pricing," said a trader in New York.
Momentum for the Russian Eurobond picked up after the London roadshow last Friday which was attended by around 450 investors, an unprecedented attendance for a Eurobond issue.
Russia's finance minister Alexander Livshits said he wanted the Eurobond to show the country was a respectable borrower.
The deal has been mentioned for the past couple of years.

With the mandate awarded in February, the Russian presidential election in the summer and a clutch of credit ratings in October, Russian President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery earlier this month was the final major hurdle.
